Example 1.3.2: expected mean squares in the fixed and the mixed model

Source: R/examples.R
Examp1.3.2.Rd

Drugs are given to whole herds and doses to animals within herds (ex124). With herd random, drug is tested against herd within drug (Table 1.3.2.2); with one observation deleted the two expected mean squares no longer match (Table 1.3.2.3: 9.7143 and 9.7222), so the F test is only approximate.

References

Duchateau, L., Janssen, P. and Rowlands, G. J. (1998). Linear Mixed Models. An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research. International Livestock Research Institute, Nairobi.

See also

vlm_ems, vlm_fit, ex124

Other VetResearchLMM examples: Examp2.2.1.7, Examp2.3.2, Examp2.4.2.2, Examp2.4.3.1, Examp2.5.1.1, Examp2.5.2.1, Examp2.5.3.1, Examp2.5.4.1, Examp2.6.1, Examp3.1, Examp3.2, Examp3.3

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

# SAS program of the book (Appendix B):
#   proc glm data=ex124;
#     class herd dose drug;
#     model PCVdif = drug herd(drug) dose dose*drug;
#     random herd(drug) / test;
#   run;

em <-
  vlm_ems(
      fixed  = PCVdif ~ drug + drug:herd + dose + dose:drug
    , data   = ex124
    , random = ~ drug:herd
    , type   = 3
    , class  = "herd"
    )
em
#> Type 3 analysis of variance of PCVdif
#> 
#> Analysis of variance
#>     source df     ss     ms                                         ems      F
#>       drug  1  1.722  1.722 Var(Residual) + 10 Var(drug:herd) + Q(drug) 0.3048
#>  drug:herd  2  11.30  5.650           Var(Residual) + 10 Var(drug:herd)  23.97
#>       dose  1  172.6  172.6                     Var(Residual) + Q(dose)  732.4
#>  drug:dose  1 0.1562 0.1562                Var(Residual) + Q(drug:dose) 0.6629
#>   Residual 34  8.014 0.2357                               Var(Residual)       
#>  den_df      p
#>       2  0.636
#>      34 <1e-04
#>      34 <1e-04
#>      34  0.421
#>       .      .
#> 
#> Error terms of the tests
#>     source           error
#>       drug 1 MS(drug:herd)
#>  drug:herd  1 MS(Residual)
#>       dose  1 MS(Residual)
#>  drug:dose  1 MS(Residual)
#> 
#> Type 3 estimates of the variance components
#>  component estimate
#>  drug:herd   0.5415
#>   Residual   0.2357
#> 
#> Sources: Duchateau, Janssen and Rowlands (1998); Searle, Casella and McCulloch
#> (1992); Satterthwaite (1946). Full references: vlm_cite(x).

# one observation deleted (Table 1.3.2.3)
em1 <-
  vlm_ems(
      fixed  = PCVdif ~ drug + drug:herd + dose + dose:drug
    , data   = ex124[-1, ]
    , random = ~ drug:herd
    , type   = 3
    , class  = "herd"
    )
em1$coefficients
#>           drug:herd Residual
#> drug       9.714286        1
#> drug:herd  9.722222        1
#> dose       0.000000        1
#> drug:dose  0.000000        1
#> Residual   0.000000        1

# the mixed model analysis that replaces it
fm <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = PCVdif ~ drug + dose + drug:dose
    , data     = ex124
    , random   = ~ drug:herd
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "REML"
    , ddfm     = "satterth"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = "herd"
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
fm$tests
#>       effect num_df den_df           F            p
#>       <char>  <int>  <num>       <num>        <num>
#> 1:      drug      1      2   0.3048095 6.363390e-01
#> 2:      dose      1     34 732.3935991 1.385997e-24
#> 3: drug:dose      1     34   0.6628611 4.212176e-01
